lineage.strategy: Changed from issuer-partnership conversion analysis to independent counterparty-primary stress testing of the newly sourced NVIDIA capital and 5+ GW deployment objective.

observedWeaknesses.observation: NVIDIA confirms a $2 billion investment and collaboration intended to enable more than 5 GW of NVIDIA systems by end-2030, but the counterparty release does not establish currently commissioned capacity, guaranteed site-level delivery, utilization, customer conversion or project returns.
observedWeaknesses.whyItMatters: Counterparty confirmation materially strengthens strategic and capital credibility while leaving the principal successor bottlenecks—power, construction, commissioning, utilization and economics—unresolved.

risks.risk: Treating the 5+ GW objective as present productive capacity or contracted revenue would inflate execution confidence; delivery remains exposed to power availability, construction/commissioning, financing and customer utilization.
The $2 billion strategic investment improves capital support but does not by itself prove attractive unit economics, free-cash-flow conversion or demand absorption for the planned capacity.

falsifiers.condition: Source-addressed site-level disclosures demonstrate commissioned capacity, sustained utilization, contracted customer demand and project economics consistent with the 5+ GW scaling path.
falsifiers.effect: Would materially reduce deployment-conversion and economics uncertainty.

improvementPaths: Track power-secured and commissioned megawatts, customer commitments, utilization, delivery cadence and returns separately from headline enabled-capacity objectives.

unknowns.unknown: Guaranteed GPU allocation, site delivery schedules, utilization and project-level returns are not quantified in the counterparty release.

recommendation: Use as source-addressed downside/execution-risk and falsifier support; do not convert the strategic investment or 5+ GW objective into Alpha numeric risk or score without separate underwriting.
